A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRB framework and CRUCB algorithm. All 30 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic bandit experiments and AntMaze reinforcement-learning results, with additional benchmark results and exploration heatmaps in the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original synthetic and AntMaze experiments and additionally reports a toy experiment and path- and edge-level exploration analyses.

M1.justification: CRUCB retains the same initialization, sliding-window mean and slope estimator, exploration bonus, and combinatorial Solver selection. The Future-UCB terminology and expanded explanation describe an algebraically equivalent procedure.

E1.justification: V3 Figure 1 adds a two-path routing scenario with a mandatory, slowly rising shared edge and distinct early-peaker and late-bloomer edges. Previous easy/complex routing, matching, spanning-tree, k-MAX, and AntMaze coverage is retained across the main text and appendices.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain R-ed-UCB, SW-UCB, SW-TS, SW-CUCB, and SW-CTS. The new toy comparison uses two existing baselines, R-ed-UCB and SW-CUCB; no new competing method or substantive baseline redesign is established.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises AntMaze-easy's reported base-arm count from 14 to 7, while retaining three paths and maximum super-arm size five. V3 also introduces the three-arm, two-path toy evaluation through 500K episodes. Existing AntMaze budgets and Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns from the count correction.

E4.justification: V3 adds toy edge-pull counts diagnosing baseline failure and Appendix G Figures 15–16 examining path- and edge-level attempt frequencies at episodes 100, 500, and 3000. These extend the visitation heatmap analysis already present in v2.

E5.justification: Retained synthetic benchmarks report means and 99% confidence intervals over five runs, and AntMaze benchmarks retain three runs with 99% intervals. No new seed information, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Path-easy's reported curves change: CRUCB's terminal regret at 300K episodes increases from approximately 10,000 in v2 Figure 11a to 19,000 in v3 Figure 5a under the same reported graph and growth settings; it remains best. V3 also adds toy regret/pull-count results and path/edge attempt heatmaps.

T1.justification: V2 Theorem 3's BiLipschitz condition is replaced by bounds on the reward relative to an additive sum in v3 Theorem 2, substantively revising the constant-policy guarantee's assumptions. The constrained lower-bound theorem narrows c > 1 to 1 < c < 2. Appendix C.5 also replaces v2's asymptotic expansion with a substantially revised sum-based derivation and corrects the definition of the shared pull-count quantity M.

C1.justification: V3's abstract claims a matching lower bound, and its introduction claims theoretical tightness in canonical settings. V2 describes bounds that are close in certain parameter ranges. This strengthens the stated theoretical claim although the displayed upper and lower exponents still differ; the core framework, algorithm, and empirical-superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds a specific limitation concerning fixed arms and static combinatorial structure, and elaborates how shared-edge growth misleads R-ed-UCB. V2's discussion of decreasing cumulative regret and horizon-dependent optimal constant paths is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix F.3 newly specifies spanning-tree edge cost as 1 minus outcome. Baseline pseudocode corrects initialization indices to cover the super-arm set, and Table 1 supplies toy and k-MAX specifications. Existing AntMaze hyperparameters and the description of using Yoon et al.'s code without adaptive grid refinement are retained.

R1.justification: V2's broad related-work taxonomy is replaced by a focused Appendix B comparison, including graph-triggered rising bandits and newer rising-bandit studies. V3 substantively positions CRB as more general than graph-triggered formulations and adds a first explicit rigorous upper/lower-bound comparison claim.

P1.justification: The introduction, formulation, method explanation, theoretical discussion, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work and k-MAX move into appendices, while the existing simple routing experiment moves into the main text. The method explanation now explicitly separates the index's three terms.

P2.justification: V3 switches the main text from two columns to one and extensively regroups figures by task and easy/complex setting. It redraws graphs, revises legends and markers, removes the separate early-regret zoom, and adds the toy figure and two attempt-frequency heatmap figures.

improvement.justification: V3 improves the constant-policy assumption, mechanism explanation, and exploration diagnostics. However, the rewritten lower-bound proof introduces a consequential algebraic gap: Appendix C.5 Equation (155) contains an uncancelled linear-in-T term that disappears in Equation (156), which also introduces an undefined c2. These problems in the replacement for v2's asymptotic derivation undermine confidence in a central theoretical contribution. The explanatory gains and theoretical concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
